slides.texte_overlay:
What to do when a friend
always cancels on you
Don't assume the worst straight away. Work, family or mental health can make people cancel. Ask kindly if everything is okay before you judge.
Say how it feels, once and calmly. "I miss seeing you, and the last few plans fell through. Is it a busy period?" Honest words often fix more than silence.
Make plans easier to keep. Shorter meetups, closer to their home, at times that suit them. Sometimes the plan is the problem, not the friendship.
Stop being the only one who invites. Give them space to come back to you. Their reaction tells you a lot about where the friendship really is.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. A full, interesting life makes cancelled plans hurt much less.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. A full, interesting life makes cancelled plans hurt much less.

slides.texte_overlay: Invest in the friends who show up. Time and energy are limited. Give more of them to the people who make the effort too.
Let it change without drama. Some friendships become lighter over time. You can keep the good memories without forcing anything.
